title: Thresholded Burst Shelf and Priority Attenuator - PRD Sketch
summary: This doc proposes a lightweight feature for Dedicated capacity that combines a thresholded 'shelf' (short-term reserve) with a per-tenant priority attenuator. The goal is to let tenants survive short microbursts without requiring large, persistent reserved capacity while preserving SLOs for high-priority traffic and reducing noisy-neighbor impact.
background: We get a mix of tenants: some have steady sustained traffic (reservation buyers) and others produce short, intense bursts (spiky workloads). Current Dedicated modes rely on hard reserved capacity or coarse burst credits. That either overprovisions or causes heavy eviction/latency spikes during sudden surges. This sketch explores a hybrid: a shared short-term shelf that can be 'checked out' under explicit thresholds plus an attenuation policy that proportionally degrades low-priority requests when shelf pressure is high.
goals: 1) Reduce immediate 95/99th-token-latency spikes for bursty tenants without forcing long-term capacity commits. 2) Provide bounded cost exposure for Redwood (shelf consumption billing with caps). 3) Maintain predictable latency for high-priority requests via priority attenuation and graceful degradation. 4) Simple operator model: runtime-level enforcement + product-configurable knobs.
non_goals: 1) Replace Reserved Capacity contracts. 2) Full multi-region spillover orchestration in v1. 3) Deep per-model kernel optimization—this is an allocation and admission policy layer only.
constraints: - Must not break existing SLO guarantees for Reserved capacity buyers. - Should be implementable using existing capacity broker hooks and request admission points. - Billing model must be auditable at token/request granularity. - Avoid large persistent memory / KV state per request.
high_level_design:
Core concepts: 
- Shelf (short-term reservoir): a pool of pre-warmed, low-duration capacity units (e.g., N GPU-second credits) allocated at cluster level. Units are borrowed by tenants when their instantaneous queue exceeds a tenant-local threshold. Shelf has global caps and per-tenant caps.
- Thresholds: per-tenant configurable thresholds (concurrency or queue-length) and a global pressure curve (Green/Amber/Red).
- Priority Attenuator: when shelf pressure crosses configurable bands, low-priority requests (user-set priority tag) receive attenuated execution: lower concurrency, constrained max-seq, token-sampling, or a token-cost multiplier. High-priority requests are spared until upper bands.
- Accounting: shelf borrow events are logged as short-term credits; billing converts credits into usage invoices with a multiplier. Repeated heavy borrowers get recommended to convert to Reserved capacity.
Implementation sketch: request enters admission -> check tenant queue/latency -> if above tenant threshold and shelf not exhausted, attempt shelf borrow -> if borrow approved, route to shelf lane (short-lived prewarmed pod). If borrow denied or shelf pressure high, pass into priority attenuator to degrade lower-priority requests per policy.
Key knobs: shelf_size (global), per_tenant_shelf_cap, green/amber/red thresholds, attenuation_factors by priority band, borrowTTL (max lifetime for shelf borrow), billing_multiplier.
flow_examples: Example A - small spike: Tenant A suddenly X10 requests for 90s; tenant_local_threshold=20; shelf available -> 30 shelf units borrowed; high-priority requests unaffected; low-priority requests get minor attenuation (e.g., reduce max seq length by 25%); latency restored within 200ms SLO.

Example B - cross-tenant surge: Two tenants spike; shelf enters Amber then Red; Tenant B is heavy low-priority consumer -> Attenuator reduces B's concurrency by 50% and drops long sequences; Tenant C (high-priority) continues with minimal degradation; billing shows B used 65% of shelf credits for the spike.

Example C - repeated abuse: Tenant D repeatedly exhausts shelf; after N events within 24h, automated recommendation triggers a sales/CS signal: suggest reserved swap and raise per_tenant_shelf_cap limit lowered.
api_surface: Product UI: Dedicated -> 'Burst Shelf' toggle + per-tenant threshold slider + priority mapping; CLI / API: POST /v1/dedicated/tenants/{tenant}/shelf-config {thresholds, priority_map, per_tenant_cap}; Runtime flags: --shelf-size, --attenuation-bands. Telemetry: shelf.borrow.start, shelf.borrow.end, shelf.rejected, attenuator.apply events exported to tracing and metrics.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (lab): simulate on staging with synthetic spiky tenants (1 week). Phase 1 (canary): enable shelf in a single dedicated pool with opt-in tenants; collect metrics 2 weeks. Phase 2: gated release to clusters, default-off but opt-in via API; enable automatic notifications to CS for heavy borrowers (1 month). Phase 3: gradually enable as default soft-fallback with conservative caps and allow sales conversion flows. Add guardrails: automatic disable if shelf borrow error rate > 1% or if latency regressions detected.
metrics_and_slos: Primary metrics: 95/99 token latency per-tenant, shelf.credit_consumption_rate, shelf.borrow_fail_rate, attenuator.apply_rate, cost_per_borrowed_unit. SLOs: no >2x increase in 95th latency for reserved buyers; shelf.borrow_fail_rate < 0.5% in canary; attenuator.apply_rate should correlate with reduced latency tail. Business metric: conversion rate of heavy borrowers to Reserved offers.
open_risks_and_unknowns:
- How to fairly allocate shelf under many simultaneous spikes (lottery vs proportional)?
- Attack surface: tenants could craft many short requests to game the shelf. Need anti-abuse heuristics.
- Billing disputes: users may contest shelf billing for transient events. Need clear logs and explanations.
- Implementation complexity around prewarming separate lane pods vs reusing existing warm pools.
- Interaction with autoscaler: shelf borrow spikes might trigger autoscaler churn; define backpressure / cooldown heuristics.
next_steps: 1) Engineering spike: prototype shelf broker + attenuator shim in serving-runtime (2 weeks). 2) Define billing model + legal review (CS + Finance) (1 week). 3) Confluence writeup + demo runbook + SRE runbook for rollback (1 week). 4) Setup staging experiments and add load generators for mixed-priority traffic. 5) Sync with Sales/CS to define messaging and conversion incentives.
notes_to_self: Keep initial shelf conservative; prefer false negatives (reject shelf) over impacting reserved SLOs. Track correlated events (eg infra maintenance) to avoid misattributing spikes to tenants. Add a toggle to anonymize tenant ids in early telemetry for privacy checks.
